games.title: Join It Up
games.skillName: Choosing ways to join and finish
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to select from and use a range of tools and equipment to perform practical tasks [for example, cutting, shaping, joining and finishing]
games.instruction: Think about the materials, then tap the best way to join or finish.
games.hint: Not quite. Think about whether the join needs to move, hold strongly or be quick.

questions.ask: Which joins two card strips but still lets them move?
Which is the best way to join fabric for a hand puppet?
Which holds sheets of paper for a short time?
Which glue is best for sticking wood?
Which tool cuts fabric best?
What can you use to smooth a rough wooden edge?
Which tool makes a hole in card for an axle?
How could you finish a model to add colour?
Which joins two boxes quickly and strongly?

games.title: Material Odd One Out
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to select from and use a wide range of materials and components, including construction materials, textiles and ingredients, according to their characteristics
games.instruction: Look at them all, then tap the odd one out.
games.hint: Not quite. Think about what the material is like: soft, hard, bendy or waterproof.

questions.ask: Odd one out: which is NOT waterproof?
Odd one out: which is NOT a fabric?
Odd one out: which is NOT bendy?
Odd one out: which is NOT see-through?
Odd one out: which is NOT a cooking ingredient?
Odd one out: which is NOT a construction material?
Odd one out: which would NOT be soft for a teddy?
Odd one out: which would NOT make a strong bridge?
Odd one out: which would NOT keep rain off?

games.title: Criteria Checker
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to design purposeful, functional, appealing products for themselves and other users based on design criteria
games.instruction: Read it, then decide if it is true or false.
games.hint: Not quite. Think about who will use the product and what it must do.

questions.ask: A design criterion is a rule your product must meet.
If a bag must hold three books, test it with three books.
A pencil pot for a desk does not need to stand up.
Knowing who will use a product helps you design it.
A toy for a toddler should have tiny parts that come off.
A good product should work well and look appealing.
A design only needs to look nice, not work.
A puppet for a small hand should be huge.
Asking the user what they like can help your design.

games.title: Plan It Out
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to generate, develop, model and communicate their ideas through talking, drawing, templates, mock-ups and, where appropriate, information and communication technology
games.instruction: Follow the steps, then tap what comes next.
games.hint: Not quite. Think about the order designers work in.

questions.ask: Design it, then make it, then...?
Think who it is for, think what it must do, then...?
Put the template on the card, draw round it, then...?
Make a paper mock-up, test it, then...?
Sketch three ideas, then...?
Share your drawing, listen to ideas, then...?
Measure the card, mark it with a pencil, then...?
Draw your idea, then add...?

games.title: Moving Picture Maker
games.skillName: Choosing a mechanism for a movement
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to explore and use mechanisms [for example, levers, sliders, wheels and axles], in their products
games.instruction: Think about the movement, then tap the mechanism.
games.hint: Not quite. Does it slide straight, turn on a pivot or roll?

questions.ask: A card bird's wing flaps as you push a strip on a pivot. Which group?
A rocket picture moves straight up a slot. Which group?
A toy lorry rolls across the floor. Which group?
A pull tab in a book moves in a straight line. Which group?
A shopping trolley rolls along. Which group?
A card crane arm tips up and down on a split pin. Which group?
A door handle that you push down to open the door. Which group?
A picture of a fish swims along a straight slot. Which group?

games.title: Axle Workshop
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to explore and use mechanisms [for example, levers, sliders, wheels and axles], in their products
games.instruction: Read it, then decide if it is true or false.
games.hint: Not quite. Picture the wheel turning on its axle.

questions.ask: The axle goes through the centre of the wheel.
The frame of a vehicle that holds the axles is called the chassis.
A wheel with its hole near the edge rolls smoothly.
If an axle holder is too tight, the wheels might not turn.
Square wheels roll more smoothly than round wheels.
A drinking straw can be used as an axle holder.
Wheels on one axle should match in size for a car to roll straight.
Wheels turn best when they rub hard against the car body.

games.title: Bridge Builders
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to build structures, exploring how they can be made stronger, stiffer and more stable
games.instruction: Compare the choices, then tap the strongest idea.
games.hint: Not quite. Think about folding, rolling, wide bases and triangles.

questions.ask: Which shape makes a frame most rigid?
How can you make a paper bridge stiffer?
Which tower is most stable?
How do you stop a square frame wobbling?
Where should heavy blocks go in a tower?
Which is stiffer?
Which would hold more weight as a bridge?
Which of these is a structure?

games.title: Test And Improve
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to explore and evaluate a range of existing products; evaluate their ideas and products against design criteria
games.instruction: Read about the test, then tap the best answer.
games.hint: Not quite. Check the result against what the product had to do.

questions.ask: A bag must hold 3 books. It tore with 2. What next?
A puppet must fit a hand but it is too small. What next?
A car must roll 1 metre. It rolled 2 metres. Did it pass?
A boat must float. It sank. Did it meet the criteria?
Which question checks a pencil pot works?
Why do we test products?
A hat must keep rain off. Which test is best?
Whose opinion matters most about a product?

games.title: Balanced Lunchbox
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to use the basic principles of a healthy and varied diet to prepare dishes
games.instruction: Compare the foods, then tap the healthiest choice.
games.hint: Not quite. Think about fruit and vegetables, water and eating a bit of everything.

questions.ask: How many portions of fruit and veg should we aim for each day?
Which is the healthiest drink for a lunchbox?
Which snack is healthiest?
Which sandwich filling adds protein?
Which food helps build strong bones and teeth?
Which should we eat less often?
A varied diet means eating...
Which bread is the healthier choice?

games.title: Where Food Grows
games.skillName: Sorting foods by where they come from
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to understand where food comes from
games.instruction: Think about where it comes from, then tap the group.
games.hint: Not quite. Does it grow on a tree, under the ground, come from a farm animal or the sea?

questions.ask: Which group does a potato belong in?
Which group does an apple belong in?
Which group does bacon belong in?
Which group does a cod belong in?
Which group does a carrot belong in?
Which group does a cherry belong in?
Which group does milk belong in?
Which group do prawns belong in?
Which group does an onion belong in?
